summary: I followed the script and the run finished cleanly. The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, asked one worktree question before starting, and then ran all six tasks in about 33 minutes without stopping. Each task got an implementer and a reviewer subagent. The agent re-ran both soak tests itself, and they passed. It dispatched a final whole-branch review, asked how to finish, and after my scripted answer fast-forward merged into main. All 26 unit tests pass on main. It never needed a "continue" and never reported BLOCKED.
reasoning: All four criteria are backed by evidence from git, md5 checks and the session log. The agent stopped mid-plan once: a worktree question before Task 1. After that it ran through all six tasks without stopping, including both slow soak runs, then finished with the scripted merge.

observations.description: The worktree question promised 'Create .worktrees/ratelimit on branch feat/ratelimit (adds .worktrees to .gitignore on main first)', but the worktree it actually created was .claude/worktrees/ratelimit on branch 'worktree-ratelimit', and nothing was added to .gitignore. As a result, .claude/ shows up as untracked on main.

Commit 3bf2096's subject line has the trailer stuck onto it: 'feat: add sliding window limiter Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'. The final reviewer noticed it and left it as is.

After the merge, the worktree and the worktree-ratelimit branch are left behind for the user to clean up. The agent explained this and offered the commands to remove them. __pycache__ directories are also left untracked because there is no .gitignore.

Startup: the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. There was also a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt saying Opus 5 was pinned, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the banner then showed Opus 5.5.
Implementers ran on Haiku 4.5 and reviewers on Sonnet 5.5. Every per-task review finished in about 10 to 13 seconds with no fix rounds, which seems quick for a combined spec and quality review.
The agent said the Codex review steps were skipped because codex-plugin-cc isn't installed, and that each skipped range is logged in an 'ungated ledger'.

The agent ran the 12-minute long soak as a tracked background job, polling in roughly 2-minute foreground calls, so its turn stayed alive the whole time. It also re-ran the 4-minute short soak itself to double-check the subagent's result.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before implementation
criteria.evidence: Screen showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' right after my first prompt, before any Agent dispatch. In the session log, the first Skill call is '"skill":"hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development"', followed by using-git-worktrees and finishing-a-development-branch.

criteria.criterion: All tasks completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on the main checkout
criteria.evidence: On the main checkout, `git branch --show-current` returns 'main'. `git log` shows 6 commits on top of 60731db (bc20a15 clocks, 0de869c bucket, 3bf2096 window, c1385ef registry, f5d2fde CLI, 1dc6599 integration). The session log has an Agent call with '"description":"Final whole-branch code review"'. The agent's last message said: 'I merged it into main locally. It was a fast-forward from 60731db to 1dc6599, and all 26 unit tests pass'.

md5 is the same before the run and after the merge: test_soak_long.py 736022c983bd6bc8e01f6eee093154b0, test_soak_short.py 8c4e951c325ee67c09b7998b27e1fa35. `git diff 60731db HEAD --stat -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` printed nothing.

STOP: "(I checked the plan for internal conflicts first and found none.)" | question. This was the worktree prompt, shown before any task started; the question in it read 'Want me to do the work in an isolated git worktree on a new branch?'. I answered 'use whatever the skill recommends'. The only other user message in the session log is 'merge back to main locally', which answered the finishing question ('Which option?') asked after all six tasks were reported complete, so it is not a mid-plan stop. I never sent 'continue'. Per the session log, my only user messages were the initial prompt and 'merge back to main locally'; the worktree answer went through the question widget.
